all_tweets.description:
Don't build your future on borrowed rails!

Most Web3 teams only realize the risk when they hit the scaling wall.

Third-party custody SaaS feels efficient early on - fast APIs, minimal setup. But as volume grows, so does dependency: fees scale with flow, uptime sits outside your control, and compliance becomes shared risk.

Instead of compounding dependency, Gaian_hq reclaimed their rails. They moved to a Self-hosted MPC architecture deployed inside their own cloud (AWS/GCP).

Working with @fystack, Gaian ensured:
- Sovereignty: Key shares and signing logic remain within their domain.
- Automation: Wallet sweeps operate under defined, programmable policies.
- Efficiency: Cross-chain liquidity shifted from manual coordination to deterministic control.

In 2026, the durable advantage belongs to companies that own the ground they stand on.

Speed creates opportunity. Infrastructure ownership preserves it.

This means seamless custody, transactions, and institutional access built directly into the single merged platform, not siloed across old chains. It's still early (TGE is just days away), so real adoption will tell the story, but this isn't rehashing old news—it's deliberate consolidation and upgrade under one roof.  Your fair skepticism is valide, but in my opinion the updates do show active progress on unifying everything which is what the whole point of merging within $TX. Thanks!

all_tweets.title: I’ve been on several community calls over the past few weeks. There’s clear excitement, but also und
all_tweets.description:
I’ve been on several community calls over the past few weeks. There’s clear excitement, but also understandable caution. Some are asking whether the COREUM/SOLOGENIC team is simply over-promising again.

In my view, integrations like Fireblocks — along with the recent BitGo integration and exchange support announcements — materially increase credibility. These are not small retail-facing moves; they are institutional-grade infrastructure decisions.

Does this eliminate execution risk? No. No one controls macro conditions, and global events continue to affect crypto broadly.

But the evidence we’re seeing points to a structured, pre-prepared, institutional-oriented launch path for $TX — not a rushed or improvised transition.

That meaningfully lowers the probability of classic “rug” or vaporware scenarios.

Cautious optimism is rational. Dismissing tangible infrastructure progress is not.

all_tweets.description:
如果为各类申牌企业进行分类，运营/托管两分最为恰当：

🦀Anchorage 为代表的托管发行为主，主要卖的是美国合规市场准入权：
- 和 Tether 合作 USAT🇺🇸
- 和 Ethena 合作 USDtb
- 和西联汇款合作 USDPT，PT 是 Payment Token 简称
- 和 OSL 合作 USDGO，OSL 是香港合规交易所，已被 Bitget 控股

BitGo 是其竞争对手，与香港🇭🇰财团合作发行  FYUSD，目标也是类似 OSL 的 USDGO，盯上合规+企业级市场

🍤Circle 为代表的运营发行，主要用于自身“品牌”稳定币：
- USDC 合美国的规，主打合规市场和 B2B 业务
- EURC 合欧美的规，对比下已经撤出欧元业务的 Tether
- USYC 合收益的规，收益市场也在悄悄搞，只给机构用

Ripple/Paxos 也想走这条路，但是难度非常大，RLUSD 并无真正市场采用，Paxos 在 $BUSD 之后推出的 USDG 并不成功

至于剩下的产品线和渠道方，更主要是为了填补稳定币业务空白，方便开展加密时代资产入口业务。

all_tweets.description:
News from the Middle East has weighed heavily on us. With team members and partners in the region, this is not distant news for us, it touches people we know and work with every day.

At Bitunix, we are mindful that behind every account is a real person, and behind every transaction is a life that may be facing uncertainty. We are offering full flexibility and support to colleagues in affected areas.

We also recognize our responsibility to safeguard our community’s assets and uphold the security and stability of our platform, ensuring dependable access for users and partners worldwide.

Beyond business and beyond borders, what matters most is the safety and dignity of human life. We hope for lasting peace.

all_tweets.title: real time proof of reserves is a big deal. if USD1 is publishing live supply and backing onchain thr
all_tweets.description:
real time proof of reserves is a big deal. if USD1 is publishing live supply and backing onchain through chainlink and bitgo, that raises the bar on transparency. after terra and the 2022 collapses, that kind of visibility matters. regulators have been clear about this too. the IMF and FSB both emphasized reserve quality, redemption rights, and ongoing disclosure in their stablecoin guidance. so on the issuer side, this is progress

1. proof of reserves only answers one question: is the stablecoin backed?

2. it doesn’t answer the other one: what happens when that stablecoin is actually used at scale?

stablecoin supply has doubled in the past two years and more volume is moving into payments, treasury, and cross border flows, not just trading. visa’s onchain dashboards show billions in settlement volume. as that grows, the exposure grows with it. public chains make balances, transfer sizes, and counterparties visible by default and it is NOT fine for running payroll, managing treasury, or executing OTC size

so transparency at the reserve level and confidentiality at the transaction level are not opposites

this is why confidential stablecoins become more important as proof of reserves improves. if the backing is verifiable in real time, the next risk is operational leakage (competitors tracking flows, bots inferring strategy, analytics firms mapping business relationships, etc)

@0xfairblock fits into that layer because it does not change the asset or weaken reserve transparency. it works with the same USDC, USDT, or even USD1 and encrypts the sensitive parts of transfers like amounts and balances, while wallets remain visible and selective disclosure stays possible for audits or compliance

company.description:
Don't build your future on borrowed rails!

Most Web3 teams only realize the risk when they hit the scaling wall.

Third-party custody SaaS feels efficient early on - fast APIs, minimal setup. But as volume grows, so does dependency: fees scale with flow, uptime sits outside your control, and compliance becomes shared risk.

Instead of compounding dependency, Gaian_hq reclaimed their rails. They moved to a Self-hosted MPC architecture deployed inside their own cloud (AWS/GCP).

Working with @fystack, Gaian ensured:
- Sovereignty: Key shares and signing logic remain within their domain.
- Automation: Wallet sweeps operate under defined, programmable policies.
- Efficiency: Cross-chain liquidity shifted from manual coordination to deterministic control.

In 2026, the durable advantage belongs to companies that own the ground they stand on.

Speed creates opportunity. Infrastructure ownership preserves it.

company.description:
You're right—each predecessor chain had its own partnerships: Fireblocks with Sologenic back in 2023, and BitGo with Coreum in early 2024.

The key difference now with TX is full execution on integration from end to end. The team has rolled out native, unified support for the combined TX ecosystem and $TX token rather than just legacy carry-overs. This means seamless custody, transactions, and institutional access built directly into the single merged platform, not siloed across old chains. It's still early (TGE is just days away), so real adoption will tell the story, but this isn't rehashing old news—it's deliberate consolidation and upgrade under one roof.  Your fair skepticism is valide, but in my opinion the updates do show active progress on unifying everything which is what the whole point of merging within $TX. Thanks!

company.title: I’ve been on several community calls over the past few weeks. There’s clear excitement, but also und
company.description:
I’ve been on several community calls over the past few weeks. There’s clear excitement, but also understandable caution. Some are asking whether the COREUM/SOLOGENIC team is simply over-promising again.

In my view, integrations like Fireblocks — along with the recent BitGo integration and exchange support announcements — materially increase credibility. These are not small retail-facing moves; they are institutional-grade infrastructure decisions.

Does this eliminate execution risk? No. No one controls macro conditions, and global events continue to affect crypto broadly.

But the evidence we’re seeing points to a structured, pre-prepared, institutional-oriented launch path for $TX — not a rushed or improvised transition.

That meaningfully lowers the probability of classic “rug” or vaporware scenarios.

Cautious optimism is rational. Dismissing tangible infrastructure progress is not.

How do you ship institutional-grade rails, without turning security, custody, and operations into your entire company?

That’s where @BitGo fits in the stack.

BitGo is a core partner layer for teams that need:
Custody and wallet infrastructure that’s built for scale

Policy controls + approvals + auditability (the stuff serious operators can’t ignore)

A foundation that helps you move fast without compromising on trust

If you’re a neobank building the next generation of financial products, this is what your stack looks like in practice.

🦀Anchorage 为代表的托管发行为主，主要卖的是美国合规市场准入权：
- 和 Tether 合作 USAT🇺🇸
- 和 Ethena 合作 USDtb
- 和西联汇款合作 USDPT，PT 是 Payment Token 简称
- 和 OSL 合作 USDGO，OSL 是香港合规交易所，已被 Bitget 控股

BitGo 是其竞争对手，与香港🇭🇰财团合作发行  FYUSD，目标也是类似 OSL 的 USDGO，盯上合规+企业级市场

🍤Circle 为代表的运营发行，主要用于自身“品牌”稳定币：
- USDC 合美国的规，主打合规市场和 B2B 业务
- EURC 合欧美的规，对比下已经撤出欧元业务的 Tether
- USYC 合收益的规，收益市场也在悄悄搞，只给机构用

Ripple/Paxos 也想走这条路，但是难度非常大，RLUSD 并无真正市场采用，Paxos 在 $BUSD 之后推出的 USDG 并不成功

至于剩下的产品线和渠道方，更主要是为了填补稳定币业务空白，方便开展加密时代资产入口业务。

company.title: real time proof of reserves is a big deal. if USD1 is publishing live supply and backing onchain thr
company.description:
real time proof of reserves is a big deal. if USD1 is publishing live supply and backing onchain through chainlink and bitgo, that raises the bar on transparency. after terra and the 2022 collapses, that kind of visibility matters. regulators have been clear about this too. the IMF and FSB both emphasized reserve quality, redemption rights, and ongoing disclosure in their stablecoin guidance. so on the issuer side, this is progress

1. proof of reserves only answers one question: is the stablecoin backed?

2. it doesn’t answer the other one: what happens when that stablecoin is actually used at scale?

stablecoin supply has doubled in the past two years and more volume is moving into payments, treasury, and cross border flows, not just trading. visa’s onchain dashboards show billions in settlement volume. as that grows, the exposure grows with it. public chains make balances, transfer sizes, and counterparties visible by default and it is NOT fine for running payroll, managing treasury, or executing OTC size

so transparency at the reserve level and confidentiality at the transaction level are not opposites

this is why confidential stablecoins become more important as proof of reserves improves. if the backing is verifiable in real time, the next risk is operational leakage (competitors tracking flows, bots inferring strategy, analytics firms mapping business relationships, etc)

@0xfairblock fits into that layer because it does not change the asset or weaken reserve transparency. it works with the same USDC, USDT, or even USD1 and encrypts the sensitive parts of transfers like amounts and balances, while wallets remain visible and selective disclosure stays possible for audits or compliance
